<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Implements #50438. EAGLE-family speculative decoding drops the last matched prefix-cache block and recomputes it, because the drafter's KV at the block's last position depends on the token after the block. **Lookahead block hashes** put that token into the cache key, so the block is reused only when it is proven equal. The drop costs one cache unit per hit, which is 544–1600 tokens on hybrid attention + Mamba/GDN models.

## Claims

- Prefix-cache hits with EAGLE, EAGLE3, MTP, DFlash and DSpark reach `floor((N - 1) / B) * B`, the same as without speculative decoding, instead of one unit less.
- Reuse stays correct: a hit reads the same draft KV as a cold run of the same prompt. A block whose lookahead token differs is not matched.
- Works with the local prefix cache and with Offloading, Nixl, Mooncake P2P, Mooncake Store and MultiConnector (when all children support it). Multi-module MTP and other connectors keep today's block drop.
- Model runners are unchanged; no new CPU/GPU synchronization.

## Validation

**End to end** (Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B, MTP k=4, align mode, 1x GB200; this PR at `3e7b8b93f1` vs its merge base `e58f8dde7f`, before #60533 and #60695 were merged in). `vllm bench serve --dataset-name prefix_repetition` with 16 prefixes of 6,007 tokens, 500-token suffixes, 128 output tokens, 512 prompts and concurrency 16. It ran three times (seeds 0–2), resetting the prefix cache before each run:

| | `main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Prefix-cache hit rate | 72.7% | **85.0%** |
| Request throughput | 9.09 req/s | **12.43 req/s** (+37%) |
| Mean / median TTFT | 404 / 304 ms | **318 / 226 ms** |
| P99 TTFT (range over runs) | 3181–3681 ms | 2745–3725 ms |
| Acceptance length | 2.24–2.30 | 2.24–2.28 |
| GSM8K 5-shot, 1,319 q, max 4096 tokens | 0.4359 | 0.4359 |
| GSM8K acceptance length | 4.11 | 4.10 |

GSM8K is a parity check: its prompts are shorter than one cache unit, and about half of this chat model's completions-API answers fail the parser on both sides. With `OffloadingConnector` (single run), the hit rate rose from 72.7% to 85.0% and throughput from 8.93 to 11.26 req/s, with the same GSM8K accuracy and acceptance.

**Hit length** (Qwen/Qwen3.5-2B, MTP k=1, unit 544, 1,367-token prompt sent twice, same revision): `main` without spec decode 1088, `main` with MTP 544, this PR 1088.

**Draft-KV correctness.** Greedy output cannot reveal a wrong draft KV (the target verifies every draft), so the check compares the KV itself. The engine runs in-process and is stepped manually. Right after the step in which a request first hits the prefix cache, the KV of its hit blocks is read and compared per position with a cold run of the same prompt. Async scheduling is on; the hits include ones landing in the same step that computes the hit blocks.

| Model | Lookahead (this PR): block-end draft slots | Negative control (`disable_eagle_block_drop`, stale lookahead token) |
|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-8B + EAGLE3 (k=3) | 0.09–0.14 | **7.55** |
| Qwen3.5-2B, MTP | 0.19 | **14.53** |
| Qwen3.5-4B, MTP | 0.29 | — |

Values are the max abs diff in bf16.

**Tests** (GB200 via Slurm, current head `5f36a6cd20`):

```bash
python -m pytest tests/v1/core
python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit tests/v1/streaming_input/test_scheduler_streaming.py \
  tests/models/kimi_k3/test_kda_metadata.py -k "not ray"
python -m pytest tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/mtp/qwen3_5/test_mtp.py \
  tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/mtp/qwen3_5/test_rejected_placeholders.py \
  tests/v1/e2e/general/test_mamba_prefix_cache.py
```

- `tests/v1/core`: 1029 passed, 0 failed. Errors are environmental: engine start-up with GPU 0 occupied by an earlier engine in the same process (2), and the `vllm` CLI missing from `PATH` on the node (2).
- Connector suites: 2220 passed. The 6 failures do not use speculative decoding: int8 `scaled_mm` is unsupported on GB200 (2), GPU memory not released by an earlier `LLM` in the same process (2), and `test_cpu_offloading` (2).
- E2E (one visible GPU): 8 passed: Qwen3.5 MTP correctness, `test_qwen3_5_mtp_prefix_cache_reuses_last_safe_block` (OffloadingConnector), rejected placeholders (2), and Mamba prefix cache MRV1 / MRV1 async / MRV2 / MRV2 async.
- `pre-commit` (incl. mypy) passes.

<details><summary>Earlier-revision evaluations (not re-run on this head)</summary>

Qwen/Qwen3.5-2B, MTP, real `OffloadingConnector`, GSM8K 200 questions, 10-shot, two passes with APC reset between passes: accuracy 0.515 / 0.515, 0 output mismatches, acceptance length 1.925.

Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct + `nm-testing/Llama3_2_1B_speculator.eagle3`, `NixlConnector` P/D with the toy proxy, GSM8K 1,319 questions, 5-shot, two passes: accuracy 0.3215 / 0.3207 (385 output mismatches between passes), acceptance length 2.077.

</details>

## Details

**Design**

- `is_lookahead_block_hashing_enabled` (`kv_connector/v1/prefix_cache.py`) turns the mode on when all of these hold; otherwise the existing drop is unchanged:
  - `SpeculativeConfig.use_eagle_block_drop()`;
  - `VllmConfig.num_prefill_lookahead_tokens == 1`, because the key proves only the next token;
  - prefix caching, or a KV connector whose `supports_lookahead_block_hashes` is true.
- `get_request_block_hasher(..., use_lookahead_block_hashes=True)` emits the hash for a block ending at `e` only once token `e` exists, with `(block_keys, token_e, token_e_keys)` as extra keys. All KV cache groups share these hashes, since a request has one hit length across groups.
- Blocks are cached at allocation, as without lookahead hashes. At request finish, the block whose lookahead token is the last sampled one is cached from `update_from_output`.
- The scheduler clears `use_eagle_block_drop` in this mode, so the last-block drop, Mamba checkpoint back-off and replay-boundary shift are skipped.
- Content-addressed connectors (Offloading, Mooncake Store) save only blocks covered by `request.block_hashes`, which lag the computed tokens by up to one block. Mooncake Store pins a final save job at request finish for that block. Nixl and Mooncake P2P transfer the request's own blocks; for Mamba models they keep truncating the prefill side at `h(N-1)`.
- MultiConnector's children are built from per-child configs, so the factory pushes the parent's decision down to every child.

**Why it is correct.** For a block `[s, e)` the key proves the prefix through `e - 1` and the token at `e`. The drafter writes the draft KV at `e - 1` (input `(h_{e-1}, token e)`) in the step that prefills or samples token `e`. The hash exists only once token `e` is in `all_token_ids`, which never holds draft or in-flight tokens. Caching at allocation therefore never exposes a block whose draft KV is not written by the end of that step. Later reads are ordered after that write on the GPU, as for regular prefix caching.

**Limitations**

- Multi-module MTP (`num_nextn_predict_layers > 1`, k ≥ 2) keeps the block drop. Its module j at position p reads token p + j, and during decode it can read unverified drafts.
- Engines sharing a content-addressed store must use the same mode. KV events keep `main`'s shape; lookahead extra keys are `(block_keys, lookahead_token_id, lookahead_keys)`, and no field marks the scheme for external consumers. When cache blocks are coarser than `prefix_match_unit`, an event carries one extra-key tuple per block, as on `main`.
- Hybrid models lose the hit when a prompt diverges exactly at the producer's last retained Mamba boundary. After a request finishes, align mode keeps its Mamba state only at the last aligned boundary of its prompt. The lookahead key then falls back one unit, where no state is kept, so the hit is 0; the drop on `main` keeps that unit's state and hits one unit. `prefix_match_unit` does not change this.
  <details><summary>Reproducer (Qwen3.5-2B, MTP k=1, unit 544)</summary>

  P1 = S + a, P2 = S + b with |S| = 1088 and a[0] != b[0], |a| = |b| = 279; requests run one after another: P1, P2, P1.

  | | P2 hit | P1 repeat hit |
  |---|---|---|
  | `main`, no spec decode | 1088 | 1088 |
  | `main`, MTP (block drop) | 544 | 544 |
  | this PR, MTP | 0 | 1088 |
  | this PR, MTP, `prefix_match_unit=32` | 0 | 1344 |

  </details>
- Model Runner V1 skips the whole drafter when a request exceeds the drafter's `max_model_len`; not handled since V1 is being removed.

<details><summary>Changes since the first review</summary>

- Merged `main` (adapted to `use_eagle_block_drop`, `num_prefill_lookahead`, Mamba checkpoint back-off, tagged extra keys, Mooncake store-job pinning, `get_transfer_results`, SWA bounded-replay window loads).
- Renamed to "lookahead block hashes".
- Removed the per-step draft KV ACK, the platform gate, the drafter-skip freeze and the V1 deferred-finalize changes; both model runners match `main`.
- Dropped the publication fence (`Request.num_publishable_block_hashes`, output-time publication, Mamba sub-block special case); blocks are cached at allocation, validated with the draft-KV check above.
- Folded the separate lookahead hasher into `get_request_block_hasher`. It had resumed incremental hashing from the last multimodal item (the pre-#51694 logic) and could drop an earlier overlapping item from the extra keys.
- Dropped per-block KV event emission and `BlockStored.hash_block_size`.
- Merged `main` with #60533 (hybrid Mamba prefix-cache boundaries) and #60695 (Mooncake partial tails). The PR's prompt-boundary helper is replaced by `get_mamba_prefill_checkpoint_position`, which lands on the last aligned boundary below the logits token once the drop is cleared. Two merge fixes: `find_longest_cache_hit_per_group` no longer widens the lookup by the EAGLE drop margin under lookahead hashes (new test), and the Mooncake finish-time lookahead save uses the new store-job pinning.
- `test_mamba_prefix_cache`: prompts whose length is a multiple of the block keep `main`'s split; prompts with a partial tail reuse one more block. The MRV2 cases spawn their subprocess like the MRV1 ones, since a forked child cannot re-initialize CUDA after earlier GPU tests in the same session.
- Other fixes: replay-boundary retention dropped the last prompt block after the merge; P/D + Mamba + MTP applied the last prompt token twice; non-EAGLE full-attention groups used the wrong prompt-tail boundary.
- Addressed review comments (boolean ACK and publication fence removed, `self.hash_block_size`).

</details>

<details><summary>Duplicate-work check</summary>

No open implementation PR references #50438 or adds the successor token to the prefix-cache key.

- #44986 skips the pop during prefill by phase; this PR makes reuse conditional on a content-based key.
- #45614 and #48375 repair or preserve the conservative Mamba back-off; this PR makes it unnecessary when the boundary token is proven equal.
- #39171 addresses hybrid coordinator drop behavior without changing the key.

Ported this PR onto a GLM-5.2 deployment branch (MTP-5, DCP-4, MooncakeStoreConnector, `fp8_ds_mla`) and hit two bugs in the MooncakeStoreScheduler that the current test suite doesn't catch. Sharing in case they're useful before merge.

---

**Bug 1 — pending-load save range not truncated (`data.py:286` assert crash)**

`build_connector_meta`'s pending-load branch hard-codes `max_save_tokens=None`:

```python
# scheduler.py, "Handle requests with pending load specs not yet scheduled"
req_meta = ReqMeta.from_request_tracker(
    request_tracker,
    self._block_size,
    load_spec=load_spec,
    ...
    max_save_tokens=None,   # <-- here
)
```

The other four `from_request_tracker` call sites all pass `self._max_save_tokens(...)`. When `can_load=False` but `kvpool_cached_tokens > 0` (partial lookup hit that didn't qualify for load), `_request_hashes_for_meta` truncates `block_hashes` to the publishable boundary via `_publishable_hashes`, but `token_len_chunk` covers the full kvpool prefix. `process_tokens` then trips:

```
assert token_len // self.hash_block_size <= len(block_hashes)
```

All 8 TP workers crash simultaneously. External prefix cache hit rate stays 0% because every save is aborted.

Fix: pass `self._max_save_tokens(unfinished_req, load_spec)` — same as the other call sites.

---

**Bug 2 — group-count mismatch when `req_tuple[1]` is empty (`EngineCore` fatal)**

`update_state_after_alloc` stores `()` (0 groups) into `_unfinished_requests` when `num_external_tokens == 0`:

```python
local_block_ids: tuple[list[int], ...] = ()
if num_external_tokens > 0:
    local_block_ids = blocks.get_block_ids()
self._unfinished_requests[request.request_id] = (request, local_block_ids)
```

The None-guard in the cached-req loop rebuilds from `req_tuple[1]`:

```python
new_block_ids = cached_reqs.new_block_ids[i]
if new_block_ids is None:
    new_block_ids = tuple([] for _ in req_tuple[1])   # req_tuple[1] == () → still ()
if not new_block_ids and not self.use_eagle_prefix_cache_hashing:
    continue
```

With EAGLE hashing active the `continue` is skipped, so `()` flows into `RequestTracker.update(())` → `ValueError: Group count mismatch: tracker has 1 groups, update has 0` → `EngineCore` fatal crash.

Before the factory wires up `set_eagle_prefix_cache_hashing(True)` the `continue` masks this; after it propagates, the crash surfaces.

Fix: rebuild from the tracker's `allocated_block_ids` (group count fixed at prefill/resume time) instead of `req_tuple[1]`:

```python
if not new_block_ids:
    if not self.use_eagle_prefix_cache_hashing:
        continue
    tracker = self._request_trackers.get(req_id)
    if tracker is not None:
        new_block_ids = tuple([] for _ in tracker.allocated_block_ids)
    else:
        new_block_ids = tuple([] for _ in req_tuple[1])
```

---

Both reproduced locally with unit tests (`test_pending_load_miss_truncates_save_to_publishable_hashes`, `test_eagle_cached_request_empty_block_list_uses_tracker_groups`); stashing either fix makes the corresponding test fail with the exact error above. Happy to send patches if that's easier than picking from the description.]

**Ported and validated on consumer Blackwell, under a block-diffusion (DFlash2) drafter — restores prefix-cache hits on both sm120 and sm121, greedy-deterministic.**

Since this PR is the candidate that actually moves the hybrid-GDN × spec cases (per the GB10 datapoint in #52244), we ported it onto our DFlash2×NVFP4-KV line — the stack behind #53977/#53978/#53979 — and ran a paired exact-replay probe (12,812-token deterministic prompt, greedy temp0/seed0, replay + extended replay, server-side `prefix_cache_hits` deltas):

| arm | exact-replay cache hits | replay output vs cold |
|---|---:|---|
| sm120 (RTX 5090), unpatched base | **0 / 12,812** | byte-identical |
| sm120, + this PR | **11,648 / 12,812 (90.9%)** | **byte-identical** |
| sm121 (GB10), + this PR | **11,648 / 12,812 (90.9%)** | **byte-identical** |

Both architectures land on the same hit count to the token; the remainder is boundary alignment as designed. The byte-identity of cold vs replayed completions is the signal we care most about: the successor-proven boundary reuses KV without touching greedy output — on a *diffusion-style* drafter (`method="dflash"`, which routes through `use_eagle()`), i.e. outside the MTP/EAGLE family this PR was developed against. sm121 additionally ran a quantized (fp8 compressed-tensors) drafter.

Both patched arms additionally screen clean end-to-end with the cache active: GSM8K n=250 at 0.976 (sm120) / 0.972 (sm121, plus 6/6 long-context needle), 0 errors, same-config repeat determinism 5/5 on both, 77.5 / 22.0 tok/s single-stream respectively under the drafter — no anomaly attributable to cache reuse. (We deliberately don't claim a paired quality delta: our matched no-PR quality reference for this exact serve config doesn't exist yet, and the byte-identity gate above is the stronger statement anyway.)

Port notes, for whoever rebases this: against a current-main-derived base the merge has ~15 conflicts; 13 are mechanical parameter-threading vs the new `num_prefill_lookahead` plumbing, one is semantic — `KVCacheCoordinator.cache_blocks` now carries finalized-KV truncation for multi-module MTP, and the natural resolution (hashing on → this PR's full aligned caching; hashing off → finalized-KV truncation unchanged) shows no corruption signal under the determinism gate above. Happy to share the resolved branch or re-run the probe on a rebased head; our port: `TechPrototyper/vllm@integrate/dflash2-nvfp4-v4-pc50897`. Probe + raw numbers: [results/RESULT_pc50897_replay_probe.json](https://github.com/TechPrototyper/local-ai-lab/blob/master/results/RESULT_pc50897_replay_probe.json).

raw_graphql_pull_request.title: [Core][Spec Decode] Add lookahead-aware prefix cache hashing for EAGLE-style draft models

detail.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Implements #50438. EAGLE-family speculative decoding drops the last matched prefix-cache block and recomputes it, because the drafter's KV at the block's last position depends on the token after the block. **Lookahead block hashes** put that token into the cache key, so the block is reused only when it is proven equal. The drop costs one cache unit per hit, which is 544–1600 tokens on hybrid attention + Mamba/GDN models.

## Claims

- Prefix-cache hits with EAGLE, EAGLE3, MTP, DFlash and DSpark reach `floor((N - 1) / B) * B`, the same as without speculative decoding, instead of one unit less.
- Reuse stays correct: a hit reads the same draft KV as a cold run of the same prompt. A block whose lookahead token differs is not matched.
- Works with the local prefix cache and with Offloading, Nixl, Mooncake P2P, Mooncake Store and MultiConnector (when all children support it). Multi-module MTP and other connectors keep today's block drop.
- Model runners are unchanged; no new CPU/GPU synchronization.

## Validation

**End to end** (Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B, MTP k=4, align mode, 1x GB200; this PR at `3e7b8b93f1` vs its merge base `e58f8dde7f`, before #60533 and #60695 were merged in). `vllm bench serve --dataset-name prefix_repetition` with 16 prefixes of 6,007 tokens, 500-token suffixes, 128 output tokens, 512 prompts and concurrency 16. It ran three times (seeds 0–2), resetting the prefix cache before each run:

| | `main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Prefix-cache hit rate | 72.7% | **85.0%** |
| Request throughput | 9.09 req/s | **12.43 req/s** (+37%) |
| Mean / median TTFT | 404 / 304 ms | **318 / 226 ms** |
| P99 TTFT (range over runs) | 3181–3681 ms | 2745–3725 ms |
| Acceptance length | 2.24–2.30 | 2.24–2.28 |
| GSM8K 5-shot, 1,319 q, max 4096 tokens | 0.4359 | 0.4359 |
| GSM8K acceptance length | 4.11 | 4.10 |

GSM8K is a parity check: its prompts are shorter than one cache unit, and about half of this chat model's completions-API answers fail the parser on both sides. With `OffloadingConnector` (single run), the hit rate rose from 72.7% to 85.0% and throughput from 8.93 to 11.26 req/s, with the same GSM8K accuracy and acceptance.

**Hit length** (Qwen/Qwen3.5-2B, MTP k=1, unit 544, 1,367-token prompt sent twice, same revision): `main` without spec decode 1088, `main` with MTP 544, this PR 1088.

**Draft-KV correctness.** Greedy output cannot reveal a wrong draft KV (the target verifies every draft), so the check compares the KV itself. The engine runs in-process and is stepped manually. Right after the step in which a request first hits the prefix cache, the KV of its hit blocks is read and compared per position with a cold run of the same prompt. Async scheduling is on; the hits include ones landing in the same step that computes the hit blocks.

| Model | Lookahead (this PR): block-end draft slots | Negative control (`disable_eagle_block_drop`, stale lookahead token) |
|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-8B + EAGLE3 (k=3) | 0.09–0.14 | **7.55** |
| Qwen3.5-2B, MTP | 0.19 | **14.53** |
| Qwen3.5-4B, MTP | 0.29 | — |

Values are the max abs diff in bf16.

**Tests** (GB200 via Slurm, current head `5f36a6cd20`):

```bash
python -m pytest tests/v1/core
python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit tests/v1/streaming_input/test_scheduler_streaming.py \
  tests/models/kimi_k3/test_kda_metadata.py -k "not ray"
python -m pytest tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/mtp/qwen3_5/test_mtp.py \
  tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/mtp/qwen3_5/test_rejected_placeholders.py \
  tests/v1/e2e/general/test_mamba_prefix_cache.py
```

- `tests/v1/core`: 1029 passed, 0 failed. Errors are environmental: engine start-up with GPU 0 occupied by an earlier engine in the same process (2), and the `vllm` CLI missing from `PATH` on the node (2).
- Connector suites: 2220 passed. The 6 failures do not use speculative decoding: int8 `scaled_mm` is unsupported on GB200 (2), GPU memory not released by an earlier `LLM` in the same process (2), and `test_cpu_offloading` (2).
- E2E (one visible GPU): 8 passed: Qwen3.5 MTP correctness, `test_qwen3_5_mtp_prefix_cache_reuses_last_safe_block` (OffloadingConnector), rejected placeholders (2), and Mamba prefix cache MRV1 / MRV1 async / MRV2 / MRV2 async.
- `pre-commit` (incl. mypy) passes.

<details><summary>Earlier-revision evaluations (not re-run on this head)</summary>

Qwen/Qwen3.5-2B, MTP, real `OffloadingConnector`, GSM8K 200 questions, 10-shot, two passes with APC reset between passes: accuracy 0.515 / 0.515, 0 output mismatches, acceptance length 1.925.

Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct + `nm-testing/Llama3_2_1B_speculator.eagle3`, `NixlConnector` P/D with the toy proxy, GSM8K 1,319 questions, 5-shot, two passes: accuracy 0.3215 / 0.3207 (385 output mismatches between passes), acceptance length 2.077.

</details>

## Details

**Design**

- `is_lookahead_block_hashing_enabled` (`kv_connector/v1/prefix_cache.py`) turns the mode on when all of these hold; otherwise the existing drop is unchanged:
  - `SpeculativeConfig.use_eagle_block_drop()`;
  - `VllmConfig.num_prefill_lookahead_tokens == 1`, because the key proves only the next token;
  - prefix caching, or a KV connector whose `supports_lookahead_block_hashes` is true.
- `get_request_block_hasher(..., use_lookahead_block_hashes=True)` emits the hash for a block ending at `e` only once token `e` exists, with `(block_keys, token_e, token_e_keys)` as extra keys. All KV cache groups share these hashes, since a request has one hit length across groups.
- Blocks are cached at allocation, as without lookahead hashes. At request finish, the block whose lookahead token is the last sampled one is cached from `update_from_output`.
- The scheduler clears `use_eagle_block_drop` in this mode, so the last-block drop, Mamba checkpoint back-off and replay-boundary shift are skipped.
- Content-addressed connectors (Offloading, Mooncake Store) save only blocks covered by `request.block_hashes`, which lag the computed tokens by up to one block. Mooncake Store pins a final save job at request finish for that block. Nixl and Mooncake P2P transfer the request's own blocks; for Mamba models they keep truncating the prefill side at `h(N-1)`.
- MultiConnector's children are built from per-child configs, so the factory pushes the parent's decision down to every child.

**Why it is correct.** For a block `[s, e)` the key proves the prefix through `e - 1` and the token at `e`. The drafter writes the draft KV at `e - 1` (input `(h_{e-1}, token e)`) in the step that prefills or samples token `e`. The hash exists only once token `e` is in `all_token_ids`, which never holds draft or in-flight tokens. Caching at allocation therefore never exposes a block whose draft KV is not written by the end of that step. Later reads are ordered after that write on the GPU, as for regular prefix caching.

**Limitations**

- Multi-module MTP (`num_nextn_predict_layers > 1`, k ≥ 2) keeps the block drop. Its module j at position p reads token p + j, and during decode it can read unverified drafts.
- Engines sharing a content-addressed store must use the same mode. KV events keep `main`'s shape; lookahead extra keys are `(block_keys, lookahead_token_id, lookahead_keys)`, and no field marks the scheme for external consumers. When cache blocks are coarser than `prefix_match_unit`, an event carries one extra-key tuple per block, as on `main`.
- Hybrid models lose the hit when a prompt diverges exactly at the producer's last retained Mamba boundary. After a request finishes, align mode keeps its Mamba state only at the last aligned boundary of its prompt. The lookahead key then falls back one unit, where no state is kept, so the hit is 0; the drop on `main` keeps that unit's state and hits one unit. `prefix_match_unit` does not change this.
  <details><summary>Reproducer (Qwen3.5-2B, MTP k=1, unit 544)</summary>

  P1 = S + a, P2 = S + b with |S| = 1088 and a[0] != b[0], |a| = |b| = 279; requests run one after another: P1, P2, P1.

  | | P2 hit | P1 repeat hit |
  |---|---|---|
  | `main`, no spec decode | 1088 | 1088 |
  | `main`, MTP (block drop) | 544 | 544 |
  | this PR, MTP | 0 | 1088 |
  | this PR, MTP, `prefix_match_unit=32` | 0 | 1344 |

  </details>
- Model Runner V1 skips the whole drafter when a request exceeds the drafter's `max_model_len`; not handled since V1 is being removed.

<details><summary>Changes since the first review</summary>

- Merged `main` (adapted to `use_eagle_block_drop`, `num_prefill_lookahead`, Mamba checkpoint back-off, tagged extra keys, Mooncake store-job pinning, `get_transfer_results`, SWA bounded-replay window loads).
- Renamed to "lookahead block hashes".
- Removed the per-step draft KV ACK, the platform gate, the drafter-skip freeze and the V1 deferred-finalize changes; both model runners match `main`.
- Dropped the publication fence (`Request.num_publishable_block_hashes`, output-time publication, Mamba sub-block special case); blocks are cached at allocation, validated with the draft-KV check above.
- Folded the separate lookahead hasher into `get_request_block_hasher`. It had resumed incremental hashing from the last multimodal item (the pre-#51694 logic) and could drop an earlier overlapping item from the extra keys.
- Dropped per-block KV event emission and `BlockStored.hash_block_size`.
- Merged `main` with #60533 (hybrid Mamba prefix-cache boundaries) and #60695 (Mooncake partial tails). The PR's prompt-boundary helper is replaced by `get_mamba_prefill_checkpoint_position`, which lands on the last aligned boundary below the logits token once the drop is cleared. Two merge fixes: `find_longest_cache_hit_per_group` no longer widens the lookup by the EAGLE drop margin under lookahead hashes (new test), and the Mooncake finish-time lookahead save uses the new store-job pinning.

**Issue**: `num_publishable_block_hashes` starts at 0 and only advances after decode tokens are finalized, but save metadata is built before the fence advances (`build_connector_meta` runs ahead of `update_from_output`). On a cold-start prefill this publishes an empty hash list, so prefill KV is never written to distal KV stores (Mooncake L3 / offloading), breaking cross-instance prefill-cache sharing.

Prefill block hashes are suffix-bound to *finalized prompt tokens*, so they must not be gated by the publication fence (which exists to guard draft-token successors during decode). Suggest taking the max of the fence and the prefill-covered block count:
```python
prefill_hashes = request.num_prompt_tokens // self._hash_block_size
publishable = max(request.num_publishable_block_hashes, prefill_hashes)
```
Verified on TP8+DCP4 GLM-5.2 with Mooncake: cold prefill now saves prefill KV (save_put +32 keys/112MB), and after local prefix-cache reset the same prompt loads 2048 tokens back (load_get 8 ops/224MB, 0 failures).

Ported this PR onto a GLM-5.2 deployment branch (MTP-5, DCP-4, MooncakeStoreConnector, `fp8_ds_mla`) and hit two bugs in the MooncakeStoreScheduler that the current test suite doesn't catch. Sharing in case they're useful before merge.

---

**Bug 1 — pending-load save range not truncated (`data.py:286` assert crash)**

`build_connector_meta`'s pending-load branch hard-codes `max_save_tokens=None`:

```python
# scheduler.py, "Handle requests with pending load specs not yet scheduled"
req_meta = ReqMeta.from_request_tracker(
    request_tracker,
    self._block_size,
    load_spec=load_spec,
    ...
    max_save_tokens=None,   # <-- here
)
```

The other four `from_request_tracker` call sites all pass `self._max_save_tokens(...)`. When `can_load=False` but `kvpool_cached_tokens > 0` (partial lookup hit that didn't qualify for load), `_request_hashes_for_meta` truncates `block_hashes` to the publishable boundary via `_publishable_hashes`, but `token_len_chunk` covers the full kvpool prefix. `process_tokens` then trips:

```
assert token_len // self.hash_block_size <= len(block_hashes)
```

All 8 TP workers crash simultaneously. External prefix cache hit rate stays 0% because every save is aborted.

Fix: pass `self._max_save_tokens(unfinished_req, load_spec)` — same as the other call sites.

---

**Bug 2 — group-count mismatch when `req_tuple[1]` is empty (`EngineCore` fatal)**

`update_state_after_alloc` stores `()` (0 groups) into `_unfinished_requests` when `num_external_tokens == 0`:

```python
local_block_ids: tuple[list[int], ...] = ()
if num_external_tokens > 0:
    local_block_ids = blocks.get_block_ids()
self._unfinished_requests[request.request_id] = (request, local_block_ids)
```

The None-guard in the cached-req loop rebuilds from `req_tuple[1]`:

```python
new_block_ids = cached_reqs.new_block_ids[i]
if new_block_ids is None:
    new_block_ids = tuple([] for _ in req_tuple[1])   # req_tuple[1] == () → still ()
if not new_block_ids and not self.use_eagle_prefix_cache_hashing:
    continue
```

With EAGLE hashing active the `continue` is skipped, so `()` flows into `RequestTracker.update(())` → `ValueError: Group count mismatch: tracker has 1 groups, update has 0` → `EngineCore` fatal crash.

Before the factory wires up `set_eagle_prefix_cache_hashing(True)` the `continue` masks this; after it propagates, the crash surfaces.

Fix: rebuild from the tracker's `allocated_block_ids` (group count fixed at prefill/resume time) instead of `req_tuple[1]`:

```python
if not new_block_ids:
    if not self.use_eagle_prefix_cache_hashing:
        continue
    tracker = self._request_trackers.get(req_id)
    if tracker is not None:
        new_block_ids = tuple([] for _ in tracker.allocated_block_ids)
    else:
        new_block_ids = tuple([] for _ in req_tuple[1])
```

---

Both reproduced locally with unit tests (`test_pending_load_miss_truncates_save_to_publishable_hashes`, `test_eagle_cached_request_empty_block_list_uses_tracker_groups`); stashing either fix makes the corresponding test fail with the exact error above. Happy to send patches if that's easier than picking from the description.]
